title: How to Plan a China Nature Trip in 2026 (8 Things to Set Up First) | China Travel Expert
description:
China just became one of the easiest countries on earth to travel through — but a nature trip lives or dies on eight things most first-timers never set up. This is the honest planning guide: what to book, how to get there by high-speed rail, when to go, and what it actually costs — in US dollars and yuan.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro — what this guide covers
0:59 8. Book park tickets real-name, early
1:44 7. Let the high-speed trains do the work
2:36 6. Time the trip to the mountain
3:27 5. Avoid Golden Week (Oct 1–7)
4:24 4. Budget the real numbers ($/¥)
5:16 3. Set up Alipay / WeChat Pay
5:49 2. Don't try to see it all
6:24 1. Best first trip: Zhangjiajie + Guilin
7:09 Bonus tip: go up early

🧭 Expert Tip: book your parks the moment your dates are fixed — Jiuzhaigou and others are real-name and cap daily entries, so they sell out before the hotels do. Bring the actual passport you booked with.

Rough 2026 gate prices (USD at about ¥7.1/$1): Zhangjiajie ¥239 / ~$33 for 4 days (Bailong elevator ¥65 / ~$9); Guilin Li River cruise ¥215 / ~$30; Jiuzhaigou ¥190 + ¥90 shuttle / ~$39 peak; Zhangye Danxia ~¥74 / ~$10; Huangshan ¥190 peak (3-day); Mount Hua ¥160 (Mar–Nov).
